subject: Maths
title: Substitution into expressions
subtitle: Algebra — Simple Formulae and Sequences · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can substitute given values into algebraic expressions and evaluate the result.

key_vocab.definition: Substitution means replacing a letter with a given number, then working out the value of the expression.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can substitute given values into algebraic expressions and evaluate the result.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Substitution -- Substitution means replacing a letter with a given number, then working out the value of the expression.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Replace the letter with the number. Use BIDMAS to work out the answer in the correct order.
If x = 4: 3x + 1 = 3 × 4 + 1 = 13
Substitute then calculate

Key examples:
  ✓ If x = 3, then 2x = 6  (2 × 3)
  ✓ If a = 4, then a + 7 = 11  (4 + 7)
  ✓ If x = 5, then x² = 25  (5 × 5)
  ✗ If x = 3, then 2x = 23  (not joining digits)
  ✗ If x = 4, then x² = 8  (squared means × itself, not × 2)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single variable
  Find the value of 4x + 3 when x = 5
  Replace x with 5: 4 × 5 + 3
  Work out the multiplication: 20 + 3
  Add: 23
  = 23
  (Multiply first (BIDMAS), then add.)

Example 2 – two variables
  Find the value of 3a + 2b when a = 4 and b = 5
  Replace a with 4 and b with 5: 3 × 4 + 2 × 5
  Work out each multiplication: 12 + 10
  Add: 22
  = 22
  (Substitute both letters, then follow BIDMAS.)

sections.title: Two variables
sections.content:
Substitute a = 5 and b = 2 into each expression.

(a) 3a + b
(b) 4a − 2b
(c) a + 3b
(d) 2a − b + 1

sections.title: Expressions with powers
sections.content:
Substitute x = 3 into each expression.

(a) x²
(b) x² + 5
(c) 2x²
(d) x² + 2x

sections.title: Negative substitution
sections.content:
Substitute x = −2 into each expression.

(a) 3x + 10
(b) x²
(c) x² + x
(d) 5 − 2x

sections.title: Mixed challenge
sections.content:
Use the values given with each question.

(a) 3x − 2y when x = 4, y = 3
(b) a² + b² when a = 3, b = 4
(c) 2x² − x + 1 when x = 5
(d) 4(x + y) when x = 3, y = −1
(e) x² − y² when x = 5, y = 3

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✗ If x = 3, then 2x = 23
✓ If x = 4, then x² = 16
✗ If x = −3, then x² = −9
✓ If a = 2 and b = 3, then ab = 6
✓ If x = 5, then 3x + 1 = 16
